minutes.summary: The School Committee heard extended public comment on district turnover, reading scores, and school funding, then reviewed three alternative spending scenarios (financial audit, second-grade class-size reduction, or a second BCBA) for $418,000 in additional state aid to be requested at a special town meeting, alongside restoring athletic transportation. The committee voted to pursue the class-size/literacy scenario plus athletic transportation, and separately voted to commit to spending citizens'-petition warrant article 3 funds (if appropriated) on restoring middle school sports.

votes.motion: Accept the second funding scenario: restore a primary second-grade teacher, put $15,736 toward literacy professional development (middle/high school), and $10,000 toward athletic transportation (coupled with $50,000 from the athletic revolving fund), totaling the $418,000 additional state aid request.

The school committee will support the spirit of whatever the citizens' petition (warrant article 3) proposes, if funded from a new town source outside the schools' own budget, and will spend it as requested if appropriated at the special town meeting.

budget_items.what_was_said: The district received a state grant for 36 Ignite tutoring license seats at a stated per-seat cost, down from earlier spending plans of 72 and then 52 seats. Staying at the 36 grant-funded seats frees funds that are redistributed across the three proposed scenarios.
Proposes an RFP for an independent multi-phase financial audit of the schools, combined with restoring athletic transportation using town-appropriated funds plus the athletic revolving account.
The verified athletic revolving account balance as of 8/13 and year-to-date spending were given, with a revised, lower athletic transportation cost estimate due to better competition scheduling.

DBUS quoted an approximate transportation cost, rounded up for contingency; this compares to the much higher FY27 budget line originally covering both high school and middle school athletic transportation.

budget_items.topic: Scenario 2: grade 2 class size / literacy support
budget_items.what_was_said: Proposes reducing projected grade-2 class sizes and expanding literacy educator support to middle/high school, funded partly by additional appropriated dollars plus existing professional development funds.

Proposes hiring a second board-certified behavior analyst, priced higher than a teacher due to certification level, to address new DESE seclusion/timeout regulations and rising out-of-district placements.
The district cited a rising count of out-of-district placements and average per-student costs including tuition, transportation, and an added cost if a bus monitor is required.

A commenter noted the $418,000 state aid request does not account for a stated increase in school choice/charter tuition assessments, and already includes $5,541 in automatic school choice receiving tuition that does not require town meeting appropriation.

A commenter listed balances in the school choice revolving fund, special education circuit breaker, school gift fund, and after-school activities fund as possible sources to help fund middle school sports restoration.

The article proposes transferring this sum from certified free cash or available funds to the FY2027 school operating budget to reinstate middle school sports and provide student-athlete transportation.
This figure would restore middle school boys/girls basketball and outdoor track, but not cross country or field hockey which could no longer be scheduled this year.
A higher figure would additionally restore girls lacrosse and the ski team (a co-op arrangement), though the golf team could not be restored for fall.
Coaching stipends, transportation, and officials/entry fees were broken out to total the middle school sports restoration figure.
The middle school and additional high school sports figures were added together in real time during the meeting, acknowledged as an estimate that could come in lower.
A commenter cited a booster donation of this amount that helped fund the middle school jazz band after it was cut, as an example of smaller funding gaps across programs.

decisions.decision: Stay at the 36 grant-funded Ignite tutoring seats rather than expanding further, freeing remaining funds for the other scenarios.

The private-transportation waiver form will be removed from final forms if the funding article passes at town meeting.
The committee will refund transportation donations previously collected from boosters, returning the decision on use of those funds to the booster clubs.

minutes.headline: The committee voted to restore a second-grade teacher and literacy funding over an audit or a second BCBA.

what_happened.line: Committee voted to restore a second-grade teacher and fund literacy support plus athletic transportation, rather than an outside audit or a second BCBA.
Committee voted to commit any citizens'-petition warrant article 3 funds, if appropriated at special town meeting, to restoring middle school sports.
Committee decided to hold Ignite tutoring at 36 grant-funded seats rather than expand, freeing money for the other scenarios.
Committee will refund transportation donations already collected from boosters and return that decision to the booster clubs.
The private-transportation waiver form will be dropped from final forms if the funding article passes at town meeting.

why_it_matters: The vote decides whether second-grade class sizes shrink and middle/high school literacy support expands, funded from additional state aid the town has not yet appropriated at special town meeting.
Whether middle school sports return depends on a citizens' petition warrant article at that same town meeting, not on this vote alone.
Families who paid privately for athletic transportation, or donated to boosters for it, may see refunds and a change to the waiver paperwork if the article passes.
